newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly steady, Med active.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly steady, Med active.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carrier (VLCC) freight rates were little changed on Tuesday, while the Mediterranean 80,000 tonne market was active with rates steady to firmer, brokers said.

Inter-U.K./Cont rates showed a weaker tone, with 80,000 tonnes at around W100. One broker said, "There's a lack of cargoes, and a few VLCCs have been fixed from Sullom Voe (in the Shetland Islands), taking oil out of the region."

He said an inter-UKC 80,000 tonner had been fixed as low as W97.5, although rates continued to depend to a large extent on dates and specific port, with W110 still achievable from Ventspils, for example.
Med 80,000 tonne rates cargoes were fixed at W125 from Libya and the Black Sea, with Sidi Kreir 2.5 to five points lower due to few vessel restrictions, brokers said.
Delays at Milazzo and Trieste were also holding Med rates up, one added.

Meanwhile, Mideast VLCCs were steady, with voyages west and to Singapore at around W50 and to Japan at W60/62.5. West Africa rates were also unchanged, with VLCCs around W72.5 and 130,000 tonne vessels at W95.
The European fuel oil tanker market was quiet, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne cargoes slightly weaker at W190 and cross-Med flat at W205.

The Caribs/upcoast sector was no more eventful than the European market, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes a touch softer at W220 on plentiful tonnage and low enquiry, and 50,000 tonne fuel oil vessels unchanged at W220, a U.S. broker said.
